purpose: Contract governance, SDK distribution and cross-repository compatibility. Not a runtime gateway.

authority: Testagram-native access-token issuance and live-session validation
services.auth: Testagram-native short-lived access JWT; PostgreSQL session/account checks on every protected request; opaque rotating refresh token accepted only by /api/auth/refresh; no external identity-provider bearer fallback on end-user routes
services.notes: Backend remains the canonical identity, authorization, content, wallet and relationship authority. The current dependent review chain is PR #424 → #434 → #435 → #437 → #439 → #441. PR #437 adds viewer-scoped username resolution and owner-scoped M-Pesa idempotency recovery; #439 adds communication privacy/block enforcement; #441 is the fail-closed follow-up, closes additional delete/call-end policy routing gaps and removes legacy plaintext from message-list responses. All are open, unmerged candidates and the chain must be reviewed and merged sequentially. PR #440 is validation-only and must never be merged. Independent security review, exact-head CI, PostgreSQL concurrency tests and staging acceptance remain mandatory.

authority: Testagram-native login, refresh, recovery and session restoration
services.auth: Uses Backend-native login and rotating refresh credentials; stores only the refresh token in platform secure storage; access token stays in memory
services.notes: Flutter PR chain: #116 provides the consolidated social/knowledge, profile safety, deep-link, wallet and monetization foundations; #117 layers the hybrid social/knowledge UI; #118 adds direct-message and voice/video call destinations; #120 removes plaintext message rendering and adds a regression test. The current source pin is the exact #120 head and includes its stacked ancestors. Wallet and profile actions use authenticated Backend contracts. Monetization destinations are navigable foundations only; campaign, earnings, premium, subscription, boost, payout and gifts/tips workflows remain unavailable until their Backend contracts, ledger/provider reconciliation and end-to-end tests exist. Message composition and media calling remain disabled until verified E2EE and signaling/media lifecycles are implemented. Flutter native Android App Links/iOS Universal Links still require verified packaging associations.

services.auth: PLATFORM_INTERNAL_TOKEN for protected platform writes; video and notification user routes validate Backend-native access JWTs against live PostgreSQL session/account state; user tokens are never platform service credentials
services.notes: Data Centre video and notification user-aware routes validate Backend-issued native access JWTs and recheck live PostgreSQL session/account state. PLATFORM_INTERNAL_TOKEN remains separate for protected platform writes. The private media lifecycle API has a typed Backend client in native-auth candidate PR #424 and matching provider routes. Identity evidence is isolated under /internal/v1/identity-evidence/* with its own IDENTITY_EVIDENCE_INTERNAL_TOKEN and dedicated B2/R2 buckets; its provider OpenAPI contract is proposed in Data Centre PR #115 and pinned as a candidate in the bridge. Neither API has passed live staging acceptance. The generic platform config/events/audit API remains a separate service contract and no typed Backend consumer is claimed.

services.auth: Backend-issued short-lived viewer assertion for private media; separate origin and purge credentials; raw user access JWT is not forwarded as a CDN origin credential
services.notes: Backend PR #223 is merged. It replaces the legacy Nginx cache with the immutable Go CDN image (sha256:e4c014a043b761d6f84b05d3973a3a6831522b863eef08685b7ca6db17f55ce9), a persistent bounded cache, private Backend origin, distinct origin/viewer-assertion/purge credentials and cache purge-before-delete. Backend origin-matrix tests, Go security checks, race/static tests and self-hosted Compose validation passed pre-merge. The merged Backend deployment workflow's input-validation job succeeded, but its actual deploy job was skipped; no live Go CDN service or external HTTPS acceptance is evidenced. CDN issues #61/#65 previously reported media.testagram.site serving the older R2 Worker; custom-domain/DNS cutover and rollback still require direct verification. Cloudflare deployment/DNS credentials are not available through the current repository integration. CDN viewer assertions remain distinct from user access JWTs and origin/purge credentials; CDN never becomes the identity or visibility authority.

authority: signed delivery of Backend-authorized public Create activities
public dereferencing of Backend-canonical ActivityPub Notes
AT Protocol public author-feed adapter and DID allowlist projection
services.auth: Public ActivityPub ingress uses HTTP Signatures; Backend-to-Federation uses a distinct service bearer; Federation-to-Backend uses a different service bearer
services.notes: Federation remains a protocol adapter, not the identity or visibility authority. ActivityPub and AT Protocol are separate protocol implementations. The private Backend bridge now has a provider OpenAPI candidate in PR #53 covering durable ActivityPub activity enqueue, Backend-authorized remote-object pages and Backend-authorized ATProto author feeds, and protocol-native remote identity verification for pending ActivityPub/Bluesky subscriptions. The Backend client supplies actor URI/DID allowlists and revalidates returned provenance; Federation must not select viewer follows or create local Testagram identities. PR #53 is pinned for cross-organ contract audit but is not merged; staging service-auth, timeout/fallback and load acceptance remain pending.

authority: ranking order and ranking scores only
ranking of Backend-authorized public hashtag candidates
services.notes: Backend submits at most 200 already-authorized feed candidates to POST /v1/feed/rank and at most 200 Backend-authorized public hashtag candidates to POST /v1/topics/rank, requesting at most 50 results. The pinned Backend client, Algorithm handlers and OpenAPI agree on both routes, API-version/service-bearer headers and bounded inputs. Backend rejects unknown/duplicate IDs and rechecks current authorization before hydration. Staging service-authentication, timeout/fallback and load acceptance remain required.
